pageTitle: Klacks for Ireland | Care Rostering Without the Staffing-Crisis Chaos

hero.badge: For private care homes and home-care providers in Ireland
hero.titleHtml: The HSE staffing crisis hits your private care service — not a national HR system.
hero.subtitle: Over 6,500 unfilled HSE posts push more pressure onto private care homes and home-care providers who roster on their own. The Organisation of Working Time Act 1997 requires averaging the 48-hour week — in hospital-type settings often over a 6-month rather than 4-month period. Klacks makes that proof manageable over months, not weeks.
hero.screenshotCaption: Screenshot shown in German — the core app interface ships in German, English, French and Italian; the Klacksy AI assistant additionally understands English.

challenges.eyebrow: The everyday reality of Irish care
challenges.title: Proving the 48-hour week over months, not weeks

items.title: Acute staffing crisis
items.text: Thousands of nursing and midwifery posts remain unfilled nationwide — private providers increasingly cover cases the HSE would otherwise have handled.

items.title: Long reference period, gap-free proof
items.text: Hospital-type settings often average the 48-hour week over 6 rather than 4 months — a single spreadsheet slip goes unnoticed for months.

items.title: No central relief pool
items.text: Unlike the HSE, private homes have no central relief-staffing network — every absence has to be absorbed within the team itself.

openSource.title: Full data sovereignty: open source & on-premise
openSource.text: Klacks was built for sectors with strict security and compliance requirements, where sensitive staff data should never leave your own infrastructure. As an open-source solution, Klacks can run entirely in your own data centre or on secured local servers — without depending on US cloud providers. That makes GDPR and Irish Data Protection Commission compliance entirely your own responsibility to manage, not a vendor's.
bullets: On-premise sovereignty: full control over rosters, working-time records and logs within your own IT environment.
Open LLM architecture: AI-assisted scheduling suggestions can also run on locally hosted language models, so no data ever leaves for external APIs.
Auditable source code: a fully inspectable codebase for IT audits and HIQA readiness.

solutions.title: How Klacks keeps the reference period under control
solutions.subtitle: Weekly working time tracked over months, not just checked at month-end.

items.title: Recovery Engine for absences
items.text: If a carer calls in sick, Klacks instantly finds the best-qualified replacement within the team — no more working the phones.

items.title: Reference-period tracking
items.text: Klacks tracks the 48-hour week continuously across the full reference period on file (4 or 6 months) — deviations become visible before they become a problem.

items.title: BrightPay-compatible payroll export
items.text: Finished hours, overtime and allowances export directly in a format ready for BrightPay, the payroll package widely used in Ireland.

items.title: Autofill wizard for rotations
items.text: The GA-powered autofill assistant plans shift rotations while respecting the working-time limits on file.

items.title: Qualification-aware scheduling
items.text: Only staff with the matching qualification are ever suggested for a shift.

klacksy.title: Klacksy: the assistant built into your team's workflow
klacksy.text: Klacksy isn't a bolted-on marketing chatbot — it's embedded directly in the Klacks interface. Staff and schedulers ask about shifts via chat, request shift swaps, or resolve qualification conflicts within the team. A built-in skills and rules system ensures Klacksy only ever suggests changes that actually match the qualifications and working-time limits of the people involved.
